title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
The setting comes from the previous and next pages. I is a (combinatorial) segment with endpoints ω0, ω1. A 'découpage' is a finite set T ⊃ ∂I, t0 = ω0 < t1 < … < tn = ω1. It stratifies I into the n+1 points {ti} and the n open intervals I_{ti ti+1}, so the set Φ_T of strata has cardinality 2n+1.

A 'polygone subordonné à T' is any subset Φ ⊂ Φ_T, i.e. a finite union of strata. These are the constructible subsets of I adapted to T, and CΦ is the complement of Φ in Φ_T.

The page first records a duality between two operations. One is a closure-type operation, written * (or Omb° = 'ombre', shadow). The other is the complement: (CΦ)** = Φ*. The associated 'irreducible' figures of the complement are read off from CΦ.

Using the 'formule fondamentale' of earlier pages, it derives the boxed identity Cosupp°Φ = supp° Omb°Φ = supp° CΦ. In words, the 'open cosupport' of a polygon is the 'open support' of its complement.

Grothendieck then defines a support map Φ ↦ S_Φ = supp°(Omb°Φ), from P(Φ_T) to Σ_cons(M), where Σ_cons(M) is the set of constructible subsets of the ambient model M. He notes three facts:
- the map sends unions (sups for ⊂) to sups in Σ_cons;
- by the boxed formula it commutes with complementation C;
- hence, by De Morgan, it also commutes with intersections, so it is a Boolean-algebra homomorphism.
He identifies this property as the 'axiome des supports Atsupp 1', apparently the first axiom of his notion of 'atelier'.

Finally he introduces commensurability. Two polygons Φ, Ψ are commensurable if δΦ ∪ δΨ (the union of their boundary/cut points) is a découpage, i.e. both are subordinate to a common subdivision T = δΦ ∪ δΨ ∪ ∂I. On the next page he concludes that all usual operations on mutually commensurable constructible pieces reduce to ∪, ∩, C in a single finite Boolean algebra P(Φ_T) of cardinality 2^{2n+1}.

Purpose: to build an elementary axiomatic model ('atelier') of tame/constructible geometry in dimension 1. Constructible sets form the direct limit over subdivisions of finite Boolean algebras of unions of strata, and a support functor into constructible subsets of M respects the Boolean structure. This is a combinatorial toy case of the 'topologie modérée' programme.
errors: The step 'commutes with ∪ and with C, hence with ∩' is correct by De Morgan. However, the claim that the map 'transforms sups into sups' rests on definitions of supp°/Omb° from earlier pages that are not visible here, so it cannot be fully checked.

Several notations are ambiguous on this page alone: *, **, Omb°, supp°, cosupp°, and M with its pieces M0 and M1. The identity (CΦ)** = Φ* cannot be verified without them, though it is consistent with a closure/interior-type duality under complement.

ideas.what: Constructible subsets of a segment as unions of strata of a finite subdivision (polygones subordonnés à un découpage); finite Boolean algebra P(Φ_T) of size 2^{2n+1}
ideas.modern_name: Boolean algebra of constructible/semialgebraic sets in dimension 1; cell decomposition (o-minimal style)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (semialgebraic geometry); o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s)
ideas.where_published: Spirit close to the 'topologie modérée' sections of Esquisse d'un programme (1984), which does not contain this formalism

ideas.what: Duality between support and cosupport via complementation: Cosupp°Φ = supp° CΦ
Support map P(Φ_T) → Σ_cons(M) commuting with ∪, C, hence ∩, taken as an axiom ('Atsupp 1') for the notion of 'atelier'
ideas.modern_name: Boolean homomorphism into constructible sets; axiomatics of a tame-topology 'workshop'

ideas.what: Commensurability of polygons: two constructible pieces admit a common subdivision, so Boolean operations reduce to a single finite P(Φ_T)
ideas.modern_name: Common refinement of cell decompositions; constructible sets as a filtered colimit of finite Boolean algebras

missed.claim: The page is part of an unpublished axiomatisation ('ateliers', with numbered axioms such as Atsupp 1) of tame/constructible geometry built from subdivisions and support operators. It is a concrete trace of how Grothendieck intended to found 'topologie modérée' axiomatically. The mathematics itself is elementary.
missed.quote: Il en résulte qu'elle commute aux intersections. C'est l'axiome des supports Atsupp 1.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It may be of historical interest for comparing Grothendieck's tame-topology programme with o-minimality. No new mathematical result is visible on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is elementary Boolean bookkeeping for constructible subsets of a subdivided interval. Its only interest is as a trace of Grothendieck's unpublished 'atelier' axiomatics of tame topology.
transcription_corrections: 'diagonale[?] irréductibles[?] associés' is probably something like 'figure(s) irréductible(s) associée(s) : CΦ'.

'transforme toute intersection[?] (inc. Σ_Φ pour c)' should probably read 'transforme toute réunion (i.e. sup pour ⊂) en sup dans Σ_cons'. A union is needed for the subsequent 'hence commutes with intersections'.
'Cela l'axiome des supports' should read 'C'est l'axiome des supports Atsupp 1'.
'est un diapason[?]' should almost certainly read 'est un découpage', consistent with the next page: 'à un même découpage δΦ ∪ δΨ ∪ ∂I = T'.
'd'où, compte tenu de la formule fondamentale' is plausible; the underlined phrase may continue with a further word ('...plus haut').
Struck text in the boxed formula: 'soupp° Omb°Φ' and '= cosupp° ...' are crossed out.
